This cross-sectional study included 45 patients with confirmed PAH, stratified by New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class (I-III). Patients with coexisting ocular pathologies were strictly excluded. Vessel density (VD) in the superficial (SCP) and deep capillary plexuses (DCP), foveal avascular zone characteristics, and ganglion cell complex (GCC) thickness were analyzed. These parameters were correlated with functional capacity (6-minute walk test [6-mWT]), NT-proBNP levels, and the echocardiographic TAPSE/sPAP ratio.

Results

Retinal VD in both SCP and DCP progressively decreased with worsening NYHA functional class (p < 0.05). Retinal VD showed a significant negative correlation with NT-proBNP levels (r = -0.355, p = 0.017) and a positive correlation with 6-mWT distance (r = 0.499, p < 0.001). Crucially, retinal microvascular density demonstrated a robust positive correlation with the TAPSE/sPAP ratio (r = 0.420, p = 0.004), a surrogate for right ventriculo-arterial coupling. GCC thickness exhibited variations across NYHA classes but lacked a consistent linear progression.

Conclusion

Retinal microvascular attenuation in PAH is strongly associated not only with functional and biochemical severity but also with central hemodynamic impairment represented by the TAPSE/sPAP ratio. These findings suggest that OCTA-derived vessel density may serve as a promising, non-invasive biomarker for monitoring systemic microvascular compromise and right heart function in PAH.

records.title: Optical coherence tomography in the management of diabetic macular oedema.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Optical coherence tomography in the management of diabetic macular oedema.
content.abstract: Diabetic macular oedema (DMO) is the major cause of visual impairment in people with diabetes. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is now the most widely used modality to assess presence and severity of DMO. DMO is currently broadly classified based on the involvement to the central 1 mm of the macula into non-centre or centre involved DMO (CI-DMO) and DMO can occur with or without visual acuity (VA) loss. This classification forms the basis of management strategies of DMO. Despite years of research on quantitative and qualitative DMO related features assessed by OCT, these do not fully inform physicians of the prognosis and severity of DMO relative to visual function. Having said that, recent research on novel OCT biomarkers development and re-defined classification of DMO show better correlation with visual function and treatment response. This review summarises the current evidence of the association of OCT biomarkers in DMO management and its potential clinical importance in predicting VA and anatomical treatment response. The review also discusses some future directions in this field, such as the use of artificial intelligence to quantify and monitor OCT biomarkers and retinal fluid and identify phenotypes of DMO, and the need for standardisation and classification of OCT biomarkers to use in future clinical trials and clinical practice settings as prognostic markers and secondary treatment outcome measures in the management of DMO.

records.title: Evaluating the Global Consensus on Keratoconus and Ectatic Diseases Agreements Reached on Subclinical Keratoconus.

content.title: Evaluating the Global Consensus on Keratoconus and Ectatic Diseases Agreements Reached on Subclinical Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the consensus agreements reached in the Global Consensus on Keratoconus and Ectatic Diseases project for subclinical keratoconus, specifically that posterior corneal elevation abnormalities must be present to diagnose mild or subclinical keratoconus.

Design

Literature review.

Methods

Database review (PubMed) was performed on January 2, 2024, to identify studies evaluating the ability of posterior corneal surface metrics to identify subclinical keratoconus using the following search terms: posterior corneal elevation; keratoconus screening; corneal ectasia; subclinical keratoconus; keratoconus suspect; and asymmetric keratoconus. Articles were included for final analysis if they evaluated the ability of the posterior corneal surface to identify subclinical keratoconus compared to anterior corneal surface and/or thickness metrics and reported area under the receiver operating curve (AUROC) data for multiple variables to allow for metric comparison. Metrics evaluated in each manuscript were categorized as anterior surface, thickness, or posterior surface. The relative discriminative performance of anterior surface (A), thickness (T), posterior surface (P), and the multimetric D score (D) metrics were evaluated based on AUROC, sensitivity, and specificity in differentiating subclinical keratoconus from normal controls were evaluated.

Results

There were 29 articles identified that met the inclusion criteria and were evaluated. In intrastudy comparison, anterior surface metrics (37.9%) and thickness metrics (39.2%) performed best at differentiating subclinical keratoconus from normal corneas, while only 4 out of 29 studies (13.8%) reported posterior metrics outperforming all metrics. In the subgroup analysis including the multimetric D score (n = 15), anterior surface metrics performed best (33.3%), followed by the D score (26.7%). In this D subgroup, no paper reported superior posterior metric performance.

Conclusions

In aggregate, posterior corneal surface metrics performed worse than anterior corneal and thickness metrics in differentiating subclinical keratoconic eyes from normal controls. These results demonstrate a lack of evidence to support the consensus claim that posterior elevation abnormalities must be present to diagnose subclinical keratoconus.

records.title: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS FOR OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY IN AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.

content.title: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF DEEP LEARNING APPLICATIONS FOR OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY IN AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To survey the current literature regarding applications of deep learning to optical coherence tomography in age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

Methods

A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses systematic review was conducted from January 1, 2000, to May 9, 2021, using PubMed and EMBASE databases. Original research investigations that applied deep learning to optical coherence tomography in patients with AMD or features of AMD (choroidal neovascularization, geographic atrophy, and drusen) were included. Summary statements, data set characteristics, and performance metrics were extracted from included articles for analysis.

Results

We identified 95 articles for this review. The majority of articles fell into one of six categories: 1) classification of AMD or AMD biomarkers (n = 40); 2) segmentation of AMD biomarkers (n = 20); 3) segmentation of retinal layers or the choroid in patients with AMD (n = 7); 4) assessing treatment response and disease progression (n = 13); 5) predicting visual function (n = 6); and 6) determining the need for referral to a retina specialist (n = 3).

Conclusion

Deep learning models generally achieved high performance, at times comparable with that of specialists. However, external validation and experimental parameters enabling reproducibility were often limited. Prospective studies that demonstrate generalizability and clinical utility of these models are needed.

records.title: Suprachoroidal Delivery of Viral and Nonviral Vectors for Treatment of Retinal and Choroidal Vascular Diseases.

content.title: Suprachoroidal Delivery of Viral and Nonviral Vectors for Treatment of Retinal and Choroidal Vascular Diseases.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Current treatments for retinal and choroidal neovascular diseases suffer from insufficient durability, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor-A agents. It is, therefore, of interest to explore alternative methods that could allow for robust improvement in visual acuity with fewer injections required.

Design

Literature review.

Results

Among various preclinical and clinical studies in the literature, a promising approach is the use of suprachoroidal injection with viral and nonviral gene delivery vectors. Compared with other ocular injection methods, suprachoroidal injection has demonstrated wide biodistribution of injected agents and safety as an outpatient procedure. In terms of viral vectors, suprachoroidal injection of an adeno-associated virus 8 vector expressing an anti-vascular endothelial growth factor-A antibody fragment has shown an excellent safety profile and evidence of biological activity. In terms of nonviral vectors, lipid nanoparticles and polymeric nanoparticles both demonstrate strong promise for ocular gene therapy in large animal models. In particular, biodegradable poly(β-amino ester) nanoparticles show excellent biodistribution, safety, and efficacy for gene therapy via the suprachoroidal route. Nonviral nanoparticle approaches can have notable advantages over viral vectors in terms of carrying capacity, redosability, and manufacturing costs. An advantage of gene therapy is that once a delivery vector has been optimized, genetic cargos can be readily tailored without changing the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetic properties of the delivery vector.

Conclusions

This review highlights recent progress that has been made and compares viral and nonviral suprachoroidal gene delivery for the treatment of retinal and choroidal vascular diseases. Suprachoroidal gene therapy is an emerging biotechnology that holds substantial potential to make a translational impact in treating these diseases.

records.title: Association Between Diabetic Retinopathy, Brain Structural Abnormalities, and Cognitive Impairment for Accumulated Evidence in Observational Studies.

content.title: Association Between Diabetic Retinopathy, Brain Structural Abnormalities, and Cognitive Impairment for Accumulated Evidence in Observational Studies.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the association between diabetic retinopathy (DR) and cerebral disease or cognitive impairment.

Design

Systematic review and meta-analysis.

Method

The hypothesis was formulated prior to data collection. Cross-sectional studies and cohort studies that assessed the association between any measure of DR and cerebral small vessel disease or any type of cognitive impairment in diabetic participants were included. The data were independently extracted by two investigators. This systematic review and meta-analysis adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-analyses and Meta-analysis of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines RESULTS: A total of 27 studies were included. The combined odds ratio of 5 cross-sectional/cohort studies that reported that the associations between DR and cerebral structural changes was 1.75 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.36-2.25). The combined hazard ratio of 4 cohort studies that examined the association between DR and cognitive impairment events was 1.47 (95% CI: 1.22-1.78). The combined odds ratio of 14 cross-sectional/cohort studies that examined the association between DR and different cognitive impairment events was 1.43 (95% CI: 1.06-1.93). The overall coefficient (β) of 4 studies that examined the relationship between DR and specific cognitive performance was 0.09 (95% CI: 0.00-0.18). Considering the quality of the data, we have performed subgroup analysis in studies scored >7 and studies scored ≤7, respectively, according to the Newcastle-Ottawa scale.

Conclusion

The present meta-analysis suggests that DR is associated with an increased risk of structural abnormalities in the brain and cognitive impairment. This association remained significant after adjusting for blood glucose, and the presence of hypertension, indicating that DR is an important danger signal for cerebral abnormalities.

records.title: Oral Hedgehog Inhibitor, Vismodegib, for Locally Advanced Periorbital and Orbital Basal Cell Carcinoma: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Oral Hedgehog Inhibitor, Vismodegib, for Locally Advanced Periorbital and Orbital Basal Cell Carcinoma: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review the efficacy and safety of oral vismodegib (Erivedge; Genentech) in the management of locally advanced orbital and periorbital basal cell carcinoma (BCC).

Methods

A literature search was conducted last in September 2023 in the PubMed database for English language original research that evaluated the effect of oral vismodegib on orbital and periorbital BCC. Sixty articles were identified and 16 met the inclusion criteria.

Results

Most studies demonstrated high response rates, with up to 100% of patients responding to the medication in individual studies and initial complete regression occurring in up to 88% of patients. Vismodegib treatment resulted in significant reductions in tumor volume, resulting in globe preservation for most patients. However, in 12% of patients, the response was partial. Recurrences also occurred with substantial frequency, even after an initial complete response. As such, up to 79.4% of patients required surgical intervention, and up to 23% of patients still required exenteration. Use of these agents resulted in reductions in tumor volume that may delay or prevent the need for exenteration in some, but not all, patients. Importantly, molecular analysis of tissue excised after vismodegib therapy revealed persistent tumor in all patients, with frequent accumulation of mutations that may confer resistance to further hedgehog inhibitor therapy. Although most adverse events were rated as level I or II, side effects were common, with up to 100% of patients in studies experiencing at least 1 event. Muscle cramps, alopecia, weight loss, fatigue, and dysgeusia were the most common adverse events, and several patients discontinued therapy because of them. Furthermore, 1 patient died of sepsis that may have resulted from the therapy.

Conclusions

Although level I and II evidence are lacking, most studies indicate a benefit from the use of oral vismodegib to treat orbital and periorbital BCC tumor volume. However, patients should be cautioned about the adverse side effects of treatment and the persistence of tumor cells with mutations that may cause long-term resistance. Use of vismodegib as short-term neoadjuvant therapy may be effective in shrinking tumor volume to reduce surgical morbidity while reducing the frequency and severity of side effects.

Financial disclosure(s)

The author(s) have no proprietary or commercial interest in any materials discussed in this article.

records.title: Intraoperative Aberrometry versus Preoperative Biometry for Intraocular Lens Power Calculations: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Intraoperative Aberrometry versus Preoperative Biometry for Intraocular Lens Power Calculations: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the published literature to compare intraoperative aberrometry (IA) with preoperative biometry-based formulas with respect to intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation accuracy for various clinical scenarios.

Methods

Literature searches in the PubMed database conducted in August 2022, July 2023, and February 2024 identified 157, 18, and 6 citations, respectively. These were reviewed in abstract form, and 61 articles were selected for full-text review. Of these, 29 met the criteria for inclusion in this assessment. The panel methodologists assigned a level of evidence rating to each of the articles; 4 were rated level I, 19 were rated level II, and 6 were rated level III.

Results

Intraoperative aberrometry performed better than traditional vergence formulas, including the Haigis, HofferQ, Holladay, and SRK/T, and similarly to the Barrett Universal II and Hill-RBF with respect to minimization of spherical equivalent (SE) refractive error. For toric IOLs, IA outperformed formulas that only considered anterior corneal astigmatism and was similar to formulas like the Barrett Toric Calculator (BTC), which empirically account for the contribution from the posterior cornea. In eyes with a history of corneal refractive surgery, IA performed similarly to the Barrett True-K and slightly better than other tested methods, including the Haigis-L, Shammas, and Wang-Koch-Maloney formulas.

Conclusions

Intraoperative aberrometry corresponds well with modern vergence formulas, including the Barrett Universal II, Hill-RBF, BTC, and Barrett True-K. It has greater accuracy than traditional vergence-based IOL power calculation formulas in eyes with and without a history of corneal refractive surgery.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Safety and Efficacy of Epithelium-Off Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking for the Treatment of Corneal Ectasia: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.

content.title: Safety and Efficacy of Epithelium-Off Corneal Collagen Cross-Linking for the Treatment of Corneal Ectasia: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To review the evidence on the safety and effectiveness of epithelium-off corneal collagen cross-linking (CXL) for the treatment of progressive corneal ectasia.

Methods

A literature search of the PubMed database was most recently conducted in March 2024 with no date restrictions and limited to studies published in English. The search identified 359 citations that were reviewed in abstract form, and 43 of these were reviewed in full text. High-quality randomized clinical trials comparing epithelium-off CXL with conservative treatment in patients who have keratoconus (KCN) and post-refractive surgery ectasia were included. The panel deemed 6 articles to be of sufficient relevance for inclusion, and these were assessed for quality by the panel methodologist; 5 were rated level I, and 1 was rated level II. There were no level III studies.

Results

This analysis includes 6 prospective, randomized controlled trials that evaluated the use of epithelium-off CXL to treat progressive KCN (5 studies) and post-laser refractive surgery ectasia (1 study), with a mean postoperative follow-up of 2.4 years (range, 1-5 years). All studies showed a decreased progression rate in treated patients compared with controls. Improvement in the maximum keratometry (Kmax) value, corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), and uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA) was observed in the treatment groups compared with control groups. A decrease in corneal thickness was observed in both groups but was greater in the CXL group. Complications were rare.

Conclusions

Epithelium-off CXL is effective in reducing the progression of KCN and post-laser refractive surgery ectasia in most treated patients with an acceptable safety profile.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Prevalence of Myopic Macular Features in Dutch Individuals of European Ancestry With High Myopia.

content.title: Prevalence of Myopic Macular Features in Dutch Individuals of European Ancestry With High Myopia.
content.abstract:
Importance

High myopia incidence and prevalence is increasing worldwide, and the visual burden caused by myopia is expected to rise accordingly. Studies investigating the occurrence of myopic complications in individuals of European ancestry with high myopia are scarce, hampering insights into the frequency of myopic retinal complications in European individuals and their visual burden.

Objective

To assess the frequency of myopic macular features in individuals of European ancestry with high myopia.

Design, setting, and participants

This cross-sectional analysis of the Dutch Myopia Study (MYST) and individuals with high myopia from the Rotterdam Study (RS) included 626 patients with high myopia (spherical equivalent of refractive error [SER] ≤-6 diopters [D] or axial length [AL] ≥26 mm) who underwent an extensive ophthalmic examination including multimodal retinal imaging. In addition to this combination of a population-based cohort study and mix-based high myopia study, a systematic literature review was also performed to compare findings with studies of individuals of Asian ancestry.

Exposures

High myopia, age, and AL.

Main outcomes and measures

Frequency of myopic macular and optic disc features: tessellated fundus, myopic macular degeneration (MMD), staphyloma, peripapillary intrachoroidal cavitation, peripapillary atrophy (PPA), and "plus" lesions (choroidal neovascularization, Fuchs spot, and lacquer cracks).

Results

The mean (SD) SER of the combined study population (MYST and RS) was -9.9 (3.2) D; the mean (SD) age was 51.4 (15.1) years, and 387 (61.8%) were women. The prevalence of MMD was 25.9% and increased with older age (P for trend <.001), lower SER (odds ratio [OR], 0.70; 95% CI, 0.65-0.76; P < .001), and higher AL (OR, 2.53; 95% CI, 2.13-3.06; P < .001). Choroidal neovascularization or Fuchs spot was present in 2.7% (n = 17), both lesions in 0.3% (n = 2), and lacquer cracks in 1.4% (n = 9). Staphyloma, PPA, and MMD were highly prevalent in visual impaired and blind eyes (frequency was 73.9% [20 of 27], 90.5% [19 of 21], and 63.0% [17 of 27] of unilateral blind eyes for MMD, staphyloma, and PPA, respectively). Seven previous studies in Asian populations reported a variable MMD frequency ranging from 8.3% to 64%, but frequencies were similar for comparable risk profiles based on age and SER.

Conclusions and relevance

In this cross-sectional study of a highly myopic Dutch population of European ancestry, myopic retinal features were frequent; were associated with age, SER, and AL; and occurred in all visually severely impaired eyes. The absence of treatment options for most of these retinal complications emphasizes the need for effective strategies to prevent high myopia.

records.title: IMPACT OF FLUID COMPARTMENTS ON FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A Systematic Literature Review.

content.title: IMPACT OF FLUID COMPARTMENTS ON FUNCTIONAL OUTCOMES FOR PATIENTS WITH NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A Systematic Literature Review.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Understanding the impact of fluid in different retinal compartments is critical to developing treatment paradigms that optimize visual acuity and reduce treatment burden in neovascular age-related macular degeneration. This systematic review aimed to determine the impact of persistent/new subretinal fluid, intraretinal fluid, and subretinal pigment epithelial fluid on visual acuity over 1 year of treatment.

Methods

Publication eligibility and data extraction were conducted according to Cochrane methods: 27 of the 1,797 screened records were eligible.

Results

Intraretinal fluid negatively affected visual acuity at baseline and throughout treatment, with foveal intraretinal fluid associated with lower visual acuity than extrafoveal intraretinal fluid. Some studies found that subretinal fluid (particularly subfoveal) was associated with higher visual acuity at Year 1 and longer term, and others suggested subretinal fluid did not affect visual acuity at Years 1 and 2. Data on the effects of subretinal pigment epithelial fluid were scarce, and consensus was not reached. Few studies reported numbers of injections associated with fluid status.

Conclusion

To optimally manage neovascular age-related macular degeneration, clinicians should understand the impact of fluid compartments on visual acuity. After initial treatment, antivascular endothelial growth factor regimens that tolerate stable subretinal fluid (if visual acuity is stable/improved) but not intraretinal fluid may enable patients to achieve their best possible visual acuity. Confirmatory studies are required to validate these findings.

records.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.

content.title: An Agentic AI Workflow for Automated Macular Hole Diagnosis and Structured Report Generation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Current AI models for optical coherence tomography (OCT) primarily focus on diagnosis as a standalone task. We developed and validated an end-to-end agentic AI workflow that integrates automated macular hole (MH) diagnosis from OCT images with structured patient-friendly report generation.

Methods

The proposed sequential workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent consisted of an image diagnosis stage and a language generation step. The OCT version of RETFound, a self-supervised retinal foundation model, was fine-tuned for binary classification of macular OCT scans as MH or normal macula. Training, validation, and internal testing were performed using multiple public OCT datasets with patient-level stratified splitting, followed by external validation on two independent datasets. The performance of the fine-tuned foundation model was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC). For each new OCT image, the AI agent used the trained RETFound model to classify the image, received the diagnostic output, incorporated it into a structured prompt, and called the large language model (GPT-4) to generate the clinical report.

Results

On the internal test set (n = 180), the model achieved an accuracy of 100% (95% confidence interval (CI), 97.9-100%) with an AUC of 1.00. On external validation (n = 1014), accuracy was 98.8% (95% CI 97.9-99.3%), sensitivity was 97.9% (95% CI 96.3-98.8%), specificity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100.0%), and AUC was 0.999 (95% CI 0.998-1.000). Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) analysis showed that predictions were driven by relevant retinal regions, particularly the macular hole and adjacent layers. The end-to-end agentic AI workflow generated concise and standardized patient-friendly reports for all samples, without the language model influencing diagnostic decisions.

Conclusions

This study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end AI workflow coordinated by a workflow orchestration agent for robust OCT-based MH diagnosis with a large language model for structured report generation. By separating image-based diagnosis from language generation, this approach offers a practical and scalable solution for virtual vitreoretinal clinics.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Retinal Vascular Analysis with Quantitative Metrics for Hypertensive Microvascular Damage.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: The goal of this study was to determine whether deep learning (DL)-assisted retinal vascular analysis detects subclinical microvascular remodeling associated with hypertension-mediated target organ damage (TOD) in patients with absent or mild hypertensive retinopathy (HR). Methods: This prospective study included age-comparable hypertensive patients with TOD (n = 54), hypertensive patients without TOD (n = 54), and healthy controls (n = 54). Color fundus photographs underwent DL-based segmentation using the Retinal Microvascular Health Assessment System, ophthalmologist quality review, and Fiji morphometric analysis. Central retinal arteriolar and venular equivalents (CRAE and CRVE), arteriovenous ratio (AVR), and arterial and venous network metrics were quantified. Results: AVR decreased progressively from 0.814 ± 0.038 in controls to 0.740 ± 0.043 in hypertensive patients without TOD and 0.655 ± 0.042 in those with TOD (p < 0.001). CRAE and CRVE differed among groups (p < 0.001 and p = 0.002). Arterial fractal dimension and vessel area density (VAD) declined stepwise (both p < 0.001), whereas arterial skeletonized vascular density (SVD) and diameter were primarily reduced in TOD. Venous VAD and diameter differed (p = 0.022 and p = 0.006), but venous SVD did not (p = 0.146). After adjustment among hypertensive participants, TOD remained associated with lower AVR, CRAE, and all arterial network metrics except tortuosity (all p < 0.001), but not with venous parameters. Conclusions: Retinal arterial alterations were associated with established extra-retinal TOD in patients with absent or mild HR. Residual cardiovascular confounding limits interpretation, and longitudinal studies are needed to establish temporal relationships, predictive value, and clinical utility.

records.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.

content.title: Modeling distinct pathogenesis of early- and late-onset preeclampsia via hierarchical representation learning of interactome.
content.abstract:
Objectives

We developed and validated the pathogenesis models by hierarchical representation learning of interactomes connecting endometrial maturation, placentation, chorioamnionitis, and hemolysis, elevated liver enzyme, and low platelet (HELLP) syndrome.

Methods

We utilized 19 gene sets from our previous work to infer interactomes to develop (n = 177) and validate (n = 352) explainable artificial intelligence models for each preeclampsia subtype using deep-insight visible neural network, gradient-weighted class activation mapping, and large language model.

Results

The hierarchically learned representations identified novel genes for late-onset preeclampsia (LOPE), similar to chorioamnionitis (ANKRD13A, SLA), and HELLP syndrome (PDE5A). We also identified novel genes for early-onset preeclampsia (EOPE), similar to HELLP syndrome (SWAP70, GREM2, GPR146, PIP5K1B, EZR).

Conclusions

Our pathogenesis models connected HELLP syndrome with both LOPE and EOPE. However, chorioamnionitis was only connected with LOPE.

records.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.

content.title: The association between large language model dependence and academic anxiety among nursing students: statistical indirect associations through artificial intelligence addiction and academic burnout.
content.abstract:
Background

Increasing use of large language models in nursing education has raised questions about the association between reliance on these tools and academic distress. This study examined direct and specific indirect associations between large language model dependence (LMD) and academic anxiety (AA) through artificial intelligence addiction (AIA) and academic burnout (AB).

Methods

A cross-sectional survey was conducted from March to April 2026 among 473 nursing students in Guangdong Province, China, including students undertaking clinical placements. The four constructs were assessed using items selected from published self-report instruments. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was performed with age and sex included as covariates. Direct and specific indirect associations were evaluated using bootstrapping with 5,000 resamples.

Results

Cronbach's α ranged from 0.914 to 0.944, composite reliability from 0.935 to 0.954, and average variance extracted from 0.560 to 0.721. Heterotrait-monotrait ratios ranged from 0.485 to 0.733, supporting discriminant validity. Model fit evidence was mixed: SRMR was 0.068, whereas NFI was 0.812, below the 0.90 reference value. The model explained 49.2% of the variance in academic anxiety. Large language model dependence showed a small positive direct association with academic anxiety (β = 0.138, 95% CI [0.006, 0.278], p = 0.048). Significant specific indirect associations were identified through academic burnout (β = 0.205, 95% CI [0.123, 0.303]) and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout (β = 0.098, 95% CI [0.049, 0.147]); both p < 0.001.

Conclusion

Large language model dependence was positively associated with academic anxiety among nursing students, with specific indirect associations through academic burnout and through artificial intelligence addiction followed by academic burnout. These findings highlight the relevance of problematic AI use and study-related exhaustion to academic distress. However, the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation.

records.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.

content.title: Retinal Artificial Intelligence Reclassifies SCORE2-Based Cardiovascular Risk Across the ESC/EAS Statin-Indication Boundary: A UK Biobank Prospective Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Aims

Whether a retinal artificial intelligence (AI) risk score reclassifies SCORE2 cardiovascular risk stratification in statin-naive adults across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary is uncertain. We evaluated the retinal AI risk score for 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) prediction.

Methods

In 40,672 statin-naive UK Biobank participants (aged 40-69, without diabetes), cardiovascular risk categories and treatment recommendation status (Class I or IIa vs neither) were defined using the 2025 ESC/EAS focused-update framework. Cox models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) adjusted for SCORE2 or for established risk factors. The incremental predictive value of adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 was evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation.

Results

Over a 10.0-year median follow-up (914 ASCVD events), the very high retinal AI risk group independently predicted ASCVD (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.32 vs low risk; p<0.001). Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 reclassified risk across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary (statin-eligibility NRI [net reclassification improvement] 0.012, p<0.001); reclassification was statistically significant but modest (continuous NRI 0.445, p<0.001), without C-index or net-benefit gain. In the statin-indicated subgroup, retinal AI risk groups further stratified risk (SCORE2-adjusted HR 2.16; p<0.001). Statin-not-indicated participants in the high or very high retinal AI risk groups had numerically similar observed 10-year risk to all statin-indicated, untreated participants (p=0.758). There was no evidence of effect modification by clinically detectable retinal disorder (interaction p=0.93). Incremental value was greater in women than men (sex interaction p<0.001).

Conclusion

Adding the retinal AI risk score to SCORE2 produced modest bidirectional risk reclassification across the ESC/EAS statin-indication boundary; these findings warrant prospective validation.Abstract word count: 250 words.

records.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.

content.title: Deep Learning-Based Automated Detection, Segmentation, and Quantification of Retinal Fluid on Optical Coherence Tomography: A Validation Study.
content.abstract: Objectives: To validate a deep learning-based algorithm for automated detection, segmentation, and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid on optical coherence tomography (OCT) across multiple retinal diseases. Methods: In this retrospective validation study, spectral-domain OCT volume scans from eyes with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), diabetic macular edema (DME), and macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel) were analyzed. Automated segmentation was performed using the fluid analyzer on Skopix by NetraMind Innovations, a deep learning-based framework trained to identify intraretinal fluid (IRF), subretinal fluid (SRF), pigment epithelial detachment (PED), and subretinal hyperreflective material (SHRM). Automated segmentations were reviewed and manually corrected by two masked experienced retina graders, with discrepancies adjudicated by a senior retina specialist. Scan-level detection performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and Gwet's first-order agreement coefficient (AC1). Spatial segmentation agreement across all B-scans was assessed using the Dice coefficient. Quantitative agreement between automated and manually corrected fluid volumes was evaluated using correlation and Bland-Altman analyses. Inter-grader reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). Results: A total of 98 OCT volumes comprising 31 nAMD, 25 DME, and 42 MacTel eyes were included. In nAMD, IRF detection demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.8%, specificity of 83.0%, and AUC of 0.876, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 81.4%, specificity of 96.7%, and AUC of 0.901. In DME, sensitivity, specificity, and AUC were 99.6%, 97.3%, and 0.989 for IRF and 98.4%, 96.4%, and 0.978 for SRF, respectively. In MacTel, IRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 87.3%, specificity of 95.1%, and AUC of 0.927, while SRF demonstrated a sensitivity of 86.8%, specificity of 98.4%, and AUC of 0.929. Segmentation agreement between automated and manually corrected annotations was high across disease groups, with Dice coefficients of 0.829 and 0.922 for IRF and SRF in nAMD, 0.858 and 0.941 in DME, and 0.908 and 0.97 in MacTel, respectively. Automated fluid volumes demonstrated strong correlations with manually corrected measurements, with minimal systematic bias on Bland-Altman analysis. Conclusions: The automated segmentation algorithm demonstrated strong validation performance for the detection and quantitative assessment of retinal fluid across nAMD, DME, and MacTel. High segmentation agreement, particularly for IRF and SRF, and strong volumetric agreement with expert-corrected measurements support the potential use of automated OCT fluid quantification in clinical practice and research.

records.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.

content.title: Association between deep-learning-derived retinal aging speed and rapid decline of renal function in the Japanese general population.
content.abstract:
Background

The eye and the kidney share microvascular features, and retinal changes have been postulated to reflect systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. Recently, retinal age, estimated by deep learning (DL) from a single fundus photograph, has been shown to predict cardiovascular events. The present study aimed to determine whether retinal aging speed, defined as the individual-specific annual rate of change in DL-estimated retinal age, is associated with rapid estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) decline.

Methods

We retrospectively analyzed the longitudinal data obtained from 7807 Japanese individuals who underwent repeated health check-ups with serial measurements of eGFR and fundus photographs (median 9.0 visits over median 8.0 years). We evaluated the relationship between retinal aging speed during the baseline period (from baseline to year 4) and rapid eGFR decline (≤ -3 ml/min/1.73 m²/year) during the follow-up period (after year 4).

Results

The incidence of rapid eGFR decline was significantly higher in the highest quartile of retinal aging speed than in the lowest quartile as the reference group in the fully adjusted model adjusting age, sex, body mass index, blood pressure, diabetes, smoking, eGFR, and proteinuria [odds ratio (OR) 1.34; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.06-1.68; P = .015]. In the multivariable logistic regression models, retinal aging speed was associated with rapid eGFR decline after adjusting multiple key confounders (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02-1.29; P = .027).

Conclusions

Taken together, DL-derived retinal aging speed is independently associated with rapid eGFR decline in the Japanese general population.

records.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.

content.title: Global research trends of artificial intelligence in echocardiography (1984-2025): a bibliometric analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Echocardiography has evolved substantially since its introduction in 1954. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative potential for image acquisition, quantification, interpretation, and reporting. Despite growing research interest, a comprehensive evaluation of the historical trends and evolution of AI in echocardiography is lacking. The study aimed to conduct a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the global research landscape in this field.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted using the Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection databases for publications on AI in echocardiography from inception through November 10, 2025; no language filter was applied. Data analysis was performed using Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Access, and IBM SPSS Statistics. In addition, bibliometric mapping and data visualization were conducted.

Results

Overall, 2682 publications received 35,083 citations (mean, 13.08 citations per publication), spanning 1984-2025. Original articles, conference papers, and review articles accounted for 87.4% and 98.5% of total publications and citations, respectively. Publication output remained limited until approximately 2015, rose gradually thereafter, and accelerated markedly after 2018, with similar output in 2024 and 2025. The United States led in both publication volume and total citations, followed by China and the United Kingdom. The United States also had the highest collaboration link strength, and seven of the top 10 institutions were in North America (six in the United States and one in Canada). Mayo Clinic ranked first, with 142 publications and 3604 citations, and had the earliest first indexed publication among the top institutions (1992). The journal JACC: Cardiovascular Imaging ranked first in both total citations (1,911) and citations per publication (36.75). "Echocardiography," "deep learning," "artificial intelligence," and "machine learning" were the most frequently used terms. The thematic evolution showed continuity of algorithmic-centric themes (1984-2019) with emerging clinically oriented themes (2020-2025).

Conclusions

This comprehensive bibliometric analysis highlights the rapid expansion of AI research in echocardiography, characterized by an accelerating publication output and emerging clinically oriented research topics. These findings reflect growing research interest in integrating AI into echocardiographic practice and highlight the need for future research prioritizing multicenter validation, clinical translation, and equitable real-world implementation.

records.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
records.publisher: European neuropsychopharmacology : the journal of the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology

content.title: Beyond scales: Artificial intelligence, language, and behavior in suicide risk modeling-a narrative review.
content.abstract: Suicide is a leading, preventable cause of premature mortality, yet identifying individuals at imminent risk remains difficult. There are no validated biomarkers for routine stratification, and common approaches (clinical interviews, rating scales, self-report) are limited by subjectivity, reporting bias, and weak positive predictive value for rare outcomes. Rapid advances in artificial intelligence (AI)-including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models-offer opportunities to integrate heterogeneous signals relevant to risk and treatment response. This narrative review summarizes recent AI-enabled prediction and characterization of suicidal thoughts and behaviors across major data modalities: structured electronic health records and claims; natural language processing of clinical notes and digital text; speech and facial/behavioral signals; neuroimaging and other neurobiological measures; and passive sensing from smartphones and wearables. We review common modeling and evaluation practices, emphasizing clinically relevant performance assessment (discrimination and calibration) and the importance of temporal and external validation. We also highlight barriers to translation, including class imbalance and label noise, dataset shift across sites and time, limited prospective evaluation, and the need for interpretable outputs that can support medication decisions and care pathways (e.g., triage, monitoring, and stepped interventions). Ethical and implementation challenges-privacy and consent, algorithmic bias and equity, governance, and the clinical consequences of false-positive and false-negative predictions-are discussed with an emphasis on safe deployment. We conclude with priorities for the field, including multimodal longitudinal cohorts, harmonized reporting standards, and pragmatic trials to determine whether AI decision support measurably improves suicide-prevention outcomes.

records.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.

content.title: Empirical Evaluation of Post Hoc Interpretability Methods for Clinical Trust in Deep Learning Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has been significantly improved through deep learning techniques; however, the lack of interpretability remains a major challenge for clinical adoption. Methods: This study proposes an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-driven framework for multiclass brain tumor classification using a baseline convolutional neural network (CNN) and four transfer learning models, namely ResNet50, DenseNet121, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNetB0. The models were trained and evaluated on a publicly available brain MRI dataset consisting of glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classes. Their classification performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and confusion matrix analysis. To enhance transparency and interpretability, Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP were used to visualize and quantify the regions contributing to the classification decisions. Results: Experimental results state that the transfer learning models consistently outperformed the CNN by learning more discriminative feature representations while producing more localized and interpretable explanations. The agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME, and SHAP confirms that the proposed models predominantly relied on tumor regions rather than irrelevant background information, thereby improving the interpretability and reliability of the diagnostic predictions. Conclusions: The proposed framework provides an effective and explainable computer-aided diagnosis system that supports trustworthy deep learning-based brain tumor classification and has the potential for decision-making.

records.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.

content.title: Application of an Artificial Intelligence Simulated Patient Model in Teaching Neurosurgical Decision-Making.
content.abstract:
Aim

Training in neurosurgical decision-making remains a challenging component of standardized residency training. Traditional teaching models are limited in their ability to simulate the uncertainty and complexity encountered in real-world clinical scenarios. As a novel educational tool, the potential value of artificial intelligence (AI)-simulated patient models in surgical decision-making training requires further evaluation. This study aimed to explore the application of an AI-simulated patient model in neurosurgical decision-making education and to assess its effectiveness in improving residents' clinical decision-making abilities.

Methods

A retrospective study was conducted involving 157 residents who underwent standardized residency training in the Department of Neurosurgery from January 2023 to April 2026. Based on the implementation of the AI-simulated teaching model beginning in January 2025, participants were divided into two groups according to the teaching model used: an experimental group (n = 72, receiving AI-simulated patient teaching from January 2025 to April 2026) and a control group (n = 85, receiving traditional case discussion teaching from January 2023 to December 2024). The experimental group used a large language model-based virtual patient system powered by DeepSeek to perform dialogue-driven history taking, image interpretation, surgical planning, and risk prediction with real-time feedback, while the control group received conventional methods. After teaching, an objective structured clinical examination (OSCE) was used to assess surgical decision-making across five dimensions, including localization diagnosis, surgical approach, risk identification, emergency management, and surgical timing, and a questionnaire was used to measure teaching satisfaction.

Results

The total score for surgical decision-making ability was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001). Dimensional analysis showed that localization diagnosis, surgical method selection, risk identification, emergency response, and surgical timing judgment were higher in the experimental group than in the control group (all p < 0.05). The excellent rate for each assessment dimension (>85 points) was significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.05). The satisfaction score was also higher in the experimental group than in the control group (p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The AI-simulated patient model based on a general-purpose large language model was associated with better surgical decision-making performance among neurosurgery residents. It has significant advantages in localization diagnosis, surgical approach selection, risk identification, emergency response, and judgment of surgical timing, and is well accepted by residents.

records.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.

content.title: Impact of Image Bit Depth Reduction on Deep Learning Performance in Chest Radiograph Analysis: A Multi-institutional Study.
content.abstract:
Rationale and objectives

Medical imaging typically generates 12-bit to 16-bit formats, yet conversion to 8-bit is often required. While deep learning has been widely explored in medical imaging, the influence of image bit depth on model performance is not fully understood. This study evaluates the impact of conversion from 16-bit to 8-bit for sex, age, and obesity classification using deep learning.

Materials and methods

In this retrospective, multi-institutional study, we analyzed 100,002 chest radiographs from 48,047 participants across three institutions. Images were uniformly quantized from the fixed 0-65535 range to 256 levels (0-255) with no additional processing. Three convolutional neural network architectures (ResNet52, EfficientNetB2, and ConvNeXtSmall) were trained on both 16-bit and 8-bit versions of the images. Model performance was evaluated using internal test datasets, randomly split multiple times, and an external test dataset. Statistical analysis included paired comparisons of area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) values, with Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.

Results

Across all architectures and classification tasks, differences between 16-bit and 8-bit model performance were minimal (mean differences ranging from -0.218%-0.184%). Statistical analyses revealed no significant differences in AUC-ROC values between bit depths for any model-task combination (all p values > 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Effect sizes were small to moderate (Cohen's d ranging from -0.415-0.391).

Conclusion

No statistically significant differences were detected between models trained on 16-bit and 8-bit images in the three evaluated tasks. These findings suggest that conversion to 8-bit images may reduce data storage requirements and improve data processing efficiency. Further research is needed to assess their usefulness in clinical tasks.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Breast Cancer Diagnosis, Treatment, and Perioperative Management: A Systematic Review of Current Applications and Future Perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed malignancy in women globally, accounting for approximately 2.30 million new cases and 666,103 deaths in 2022. Artificial intelligence technologies including machine learning, deep learning, radiomics, and natural language processing have been widely applied across the breast cancer care continuum. However, no systematic review restricted to primary studies with patient-level or image-level data has synthesized evidence spanning all clinical domains simultaneously.

Objectives

To evaluate the performance, methodological quality, and clinical relevance of artificial intelligence primary studies across screening and diagnostic imaging, digital pathology, radiomics, perioperative management, prognostic prediction, and natural language processing in breast cancer.

Methods

PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2015 to May 2026. Eligibility was restricted to original primary research reporting patient-level or image-level data; secondary syntheses were explicitly excluded. Risk of bias was assessed using QUADAS-2 and PROBAST. Reporting followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

Results

Of 5,275 identified records, 17 primary studies met eligibility criteria. In screening mammography (seven studies; n = 7,540 to 144,231 examinations), deep learning achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.876 to 0.939; a randomised trial in 80,033 women demonstrated non-inferiority to double reading with a 44.3% reduction in radiologist workload. In digital pathology (five studies; 270 to 44,732 whole-slide images), deep learning achieved AUC 0.985 to 0.994, exceeding unassisted pathologist performance in lymph node metastasis detection. Magnetic resonance imaging radiomics predicted pathological complete response in HER2-positive breast cancer with AUC 0.80. No breast cancer-specific perioperative primary study met the eligibility criteria. Deep survival networks achieved concordance index 0.626 versus 0.612 for Cox regression in breast cancer cohorts. Natural language processing identified metastatic recurrence in breast cancer clinical records with sensitivity 83% and specificity 73%. Risk of bias was low to moderate for imaging and pathology studies and high for small sample radiomics studies. Density-stratified performance was reported by only two imaging studies, and receptor status prediction from haematoxylin and eosin staining had not been validated as a safe alternative to immunohistochemistry.

Conclusions

Artificial intelligence demonstrated clinically meaningful performance across the five domains with eligible primary studies. Breast cancer-specific perioperative and intensive care primary studies were absent, representing the largest evidence gap. External validation, demographic diversity, and prospective clinical integration evidence remained the most consistently identified limitations. Prediction of molecular receptor status without immunohistochemistry requires rigorous prospective safety validation before it can complement standard testing.

records.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.

content.title: Digital twin oncology and multi-omics-driven artificial intelligence models for personalized drug response prediction: A systematic survey of emerging computational paradigms and clinical implementation challenges.
content.abstract: The increasing complexity of tumor heterogeneity and variable therapeutic response has intensified the need for accurate personalized drug response prediction in oncology. Traditional trial-and-error chemotherapy strategies often result in suboptimal outcomes, toxicity, and delayed therapeutic adjustments. Rapid advances in multi-omics technologies, artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin modeling have significantly reshaped computational oncology research. This survey systematically reviews peer-reviewed research and review articles published from 2021 onward that investigate emerging computational paradigms integrating digital twins and multi-omics AI for drug response prediction. The foundational concepts in digital twin oncology, multi-omics profiling and AI-driven precision medicine are outlined initially. The existing approaches are categorized into four major paradigms such as omics-driven machine learning models, deep learning based multimodal architectures, mechanistic digital twin simulation frameworks and hybrid digital twin AI systems enabling adaptive therapy optimization. The multi-omics data integration strategies, including early, intermediate, late, network-based and graph/pathway-based fusion techniques. The survey synthesizes recent developments in drug sensitivity prediction, immunotherapy response modeling, tumor evolution forecasting and virtual clinical trials, while critically analyzing challenges related to data heterogeneity, interpretability, generalization, privacy, regulatory compliance and ethical considerations. Finally, future directions are highlighted such as real-time adaptive digital twins, federated learning, explainable AI and regulatory ready clinical deployment frameworks. Overall, this review provides a structured taxonomy, comparative analysis and research roadmap for advancing integrated digital twin and multi omics AI systems toward clinically actionable precision oncology.

records.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.

content.title: Artificial intelligence analysis of oral mucosal lesions in white-light clinical photographs: A systematic review of visual features and validation.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to conventional oral photographs for recognition, classification, localization, segmentation, and risk assessment of oral mucosal lesions. This systematic review evaluated how clinically relevant visual information-including color, texture, morphology, borders, and spatial patterns-is represented by AI systems and assessed performance, validation, explainability, human comparison, and clinical translation. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for studies directly analyzing conventional white-light clinical photographs. Risk of bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI, and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation-based approaches. Fifty-three studies were included, 30 published in 2025-2026. Forty-six used implicit deep-learning visual representations, three multimodal vision-language models, two explicit color analyses, and two explicit texture analyses. Thirty-one studies primarily addressed image-level diagnostic classification/recognition, 15 spatial detection/localization or lesion delineation, six screening/triage/referral or biopsy-oriented decision support, and one longitudinal malignant-transformation prediction. Six used independent external cohorts and five compared AI with human readers. Methodological concerns were frequent, no sufficiently coherent group supported meta-analysis, and certainty remained limited across evidence bodies. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than established clinical effectiveness, with translation requiring stronger patient-level independence, external validation, prospective multicenter evaluation, and evidence of clinical benefit.

records.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.

content.title: Is Large Language Model a New Hope for the Global South? A Rapid Bibliometric Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), especially the recent proliferation of generative Large Language Models (LLMs), is transforming traditional anatomy education by introducing new teaching tools. However, the adoption of these cutting-edge technologies raises questions about global educational equity. It remains unclear whether AI will serve as a digital equalizer or further exacerbate marginalization. This rapid bibliometric synthesis aims to provide a comprehensive, data-driven overview of the "Application of Artificial Intelligence in Anatomy Education" (AAAE). We seek to map the intellectual landscape, detect structural and technological shifts, evaluate the geopolitical disparities, and provide corresponding references. A total of 85 consolidated records were retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus. These data constituted the whole panorama of AAAE. Bibliometrix and CiteSpace were utilized for static and dynamic mapping. A multidisciplinary expert panel validated the thematic clusters using Gwet's AC1 and the Normalized Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI). Publications surged following ChatGPT's release, indicating a shift from specialized computer vision to the application of general-purpose LLMs. While high-income countries maintain leadership, AI could exert a "democratizing effect" on upper-middle-income countries, doubling their odds of publication compared to traditional anatomy. Six research frontiers and three research trajectories were captured, and corresponding implications for future researchers in the global south and north were presented. AAAE could be conducted using a stratified strategy: different expansions of AI technologies for pedagogy; leveraging commercial APIs to bypass infrastructure bottlenecks; and validating open-source models. Global equity critically demands cross-border collaboration and inclusive datasets.

records.title: Diagnostic performance of plasma p-Tau217, p-Tau181, and p-Tau231 across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: a network meta-analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic performance of plasma p-Tau217, p-Tau181, and p-Tau231 across the Alzheimer's disease continuum: a network meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

Blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) are transforming the diagnostic workflow for Alzheimer's disease (AD). However, there is no consensus on the optimal phosphorylated tau (p-tau) isoform (217, 181, or 231) or analytical platform [mass spectrometry (MS) vs. immunoassay (IA)] for clinical implementation across different disease stages.

Objective

To systematically compare the diagnostic accuracy and prognostic value of plasma p-tau isoforms using different technical platforms for detecting amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology, tau pathology, and predicting cognitive decline.

Study selection

Studies reporting diagnostic accuracy [Area Under the Curve (AUC)] of plasma p-tau against cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) or Positron Emission Tomography (PET) standards were included. To ensure statistical independence, overlapping cohorts (e.g., BioFINDER, ADNI) were rigorously screened, selecting only the most comprehensive dataset per cohort.

Results

A total of 18 high-quality studies comprising 24 independent datasets and 4,736 participants were included. For detecting Aβ pathology, p-tau217 measured by MS (p217_MS) demonstrated the highest diagnostic accuracy (P-score = 0.86), followed by p-tau217 ratio (p217_Ratio) (P-score = 0.78) and automated immunoassays (P-score = 0.67-0.69), all of which significantly outperformed standard p-tau181 immunoassays (P-score = 0.12). Notably, the p-tau217/Aβ 42 ratio on automated platforms provided a significant incremental AUC gain of 0.025 (95% CI: 0.005 to 0.045; I2  = 0%) compared to single-analyte assays, effectively bridging the performance gap with MS. In disease staging, while p-tau231 showed potential in detecting early amyloidosis, p-tau217_MS was superior for identifying advanced Tau-PET pathology (P-score = 0.91) and predicting MCI-to-dementia conversion (P-score = 0.82). Subgroup analyses confirmed consistent performance of p-tau217 across Han Chinese and Western cohorts, and demonstrated the diagnostic potential of serum-based assays as a viable matrix.

Conclusions and relevance

Plasma p-tau217, particularly when measured by mass spectrometry or as a ratio on fully automated platforms, offers the highest accuracy for AD diagnosis and staging. While p-tau231 may serve as an early indicator of amyloidosis, p-tau217 is the most robust marker for tau pathology and disease progression. These findings support the integration of automated p-tau217 assays into routine clinical care to streamline patient stratification for disease-modifying therapies.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/, identifier (CRD420261327845).

records.title: Machine learning-based prediction of proximal junctional pathology after adult spinal deformity surgery: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.

content.title: Machine learning-based prediction of proximal junctional pathology after adult spinal deformity surgery: a systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Proximal junctional kyphosis (PJK) and failure (PJF) remain challenging and incompletely predictable adverse event following adult spinal deformity (ASD) surgery. Machine learning (ML) models have been proposed to improve risk stratification, but performance varies and clinical applicability remains uncertain. A systematic review and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis was performed to synthesize the predictive performance of ML-based models for proximal junctional pathology after ASD surgery.

Methods

PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to February 2026. Studies developing or validating ML models predicting PJK or PJF following ASD surgery were included. Diagnostic performance was synthesized using random-effects models, pooling sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio (dOR), and summary receiver operating characteristic (SROC) curves. A prespecified secondary analysis pooled one highest-performing model per study to reduce within-study dependence. Risk of bias was assessed using PROBAST and certainty of evidence using GRADE.

Results

Sixteen studies comprising 3625 patients and 30 ML models met inclusion criteria. Twenty-two models provided extractable test-set data for diagnostic synthesis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.51 (95% CI: 0.41-0.61) and specificity 0.84 (95% CI: 0.78-0.89), with a pooled AUC of 0.67 (95% CI: 0.62-0.72). In the highest-performing model analysis, pooled sensitivity improved to 0.63 (95% CI: 0.55-0.71) and AUC to 0.77 95% CI: 0.71- 0.83). Specificity remained high (0.86). External validation was rare, and calibration was inconsistently reported. Frequently prioritized predictors included sagittal alignment parameters, construct characteristics, bone quality metrics, and age.

Conclusions

ML-based models demonstrate biologically coherent but clinically moderate discrimination for predicting proximal junctional pathology following ASD surgery. Current performance supports risk stratification rather than categorical decision-making. Progress toward clinically actionable prediction will require standardized endpoint definitions, robust external validation, and calibration-centered reporting.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Extracellular Vesicle Platforms for Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Scoping Review and Future Directions.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Extracellular Vesicle Platforms for Diagnosis and Treatment of Chronic Kidney Disease: A Scoping Review and Future Directions.
content.abstract: Background and Objectives: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) affects roughly 788 million adults worldwide according to the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 estimate. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising sources of biomarkers and therapeutic carriers, while artificial intelligence (AI) offers tools for high-dimensional EV analysis and computational design. Materials and Methods: We conducted a scoping review using a structured PubMed/MEDLINE search, run on 7 September 2026, and PRISMA-ScR reporting principles. Eligible studies applied AI/ML to EV-derived or closely related kidney-disease data. The review was not prospectively registered. The formal scoping evidence set was used to map kidney EV-AI studies focused on diagnosis, prognosis, and biomarker discovery; EV engineering, therapeutic design, manufacturing, and physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling were synthesized separately as contextual and future-oriented literature identified through non-systematic contextual literature identification. Predictive models were critically appraised using a PROBAST-informed framework. Results: Nine reports were retained in the formal PRISMA evidence set. Direct kidney EV-AI evidence was limited and heterogeneous, with small cohorts and variable validation strategies. Several studies reported encouraging discrimination, but external validation, calibration, standardized EV workflows, and prospective clinical utility were uncommon. Contextual literature suggests potential roles for AI in EV engineering, manufacturing, and PBPK-informed therapeutic development, but these applications remain investigational in CKD. Conclusions: AI-EV integration is a promising research framework rather than a clinically validated platform. Translation will require standardized EV methods, adequately powered multicentre studies, independent validation, clinically relevant operating thresholds, prospective utility studies, and explicit manufacturing and regulatory strategies.

records.title: Estimated glucose disposal rate and cardiovascular disease risk: a meta-analysis of cohort studies.

content.title: Estimated glucose disposal rate and cardiovascular disease risk: a meta-analysis of cohort studies.
content.abstract:
Background

Insulin resistance (IR) is a key cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk factor. The estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR) is a reliable IR marker linked to CVD risk. This study is the first extensive meta-analysis of this correlation in a general population free from baseline CVD.

Methods

We searched electronic databases such as PubMed, Web of Science and Embase for cohort studies reporting eGDR and CVD risk. Studies included adults without baseline CVD, measured eGDR at baseline, and reported hazard ratio (HR) [95% confidence interval (CI)]. The combined HR and its 95% CI were determined through the application of random or fixed effects models. Meta-regression with robust error was utilized to depict the nonlinear dose-response relationship.

Results

Twelve cohort studies with 547,287 subjects were included, with follow-up durations ranging from 5.6 to 14.1 years. Participants with the highest eGDR category had a lower risk of CVD (HR: 0.58, 95% CI 0.53-0.63), stroke (HR: 0.62, 95% CI: 0.56-0.69), and coronary heart disease (HR: 0.46, 95% CI: 0.25-0.83) compared with the lowest eGDR category. This aligns with the meta-analysis results, where eGDR as a continuous variable had HRs of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.85-0.91) for CVD, 0.84 (95% CI: 0.76-0.93) for stroke, and 0.85 (95% CI: 0.83-0.87) for coronary heart disease. Subgroup analyses revealed that sex, sample size, follow-up duration, and prediabetes/diabetes status did not significantly affect the results. Dose-response analysis indicated that there was a linear negative association of the eGDR with the risk of CVD (Pnonlinear=0.120) or stroke (Pnonlinear=0.084).

Conclusions

The higher eGDR is associated with lower risk of CVD, stroke, and coronary heart disease in individuals without baseline CVD. However, the observational design and high heterogeneity across studies prevent causal inference.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Medical Devices for Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in the European Union.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Medical Devices for Diabetic Retinopathy Screening in the European Union.
content.abstract:
Background

Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable blindness, yet screening programs across Europe face persistent workforce and capacity constraints amid rising diabetes prevalence. Artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening platforms have been developed to support scalable DR detection; however, their regulatory status, validation approaches, and implementation readiness vary considerably.

Methods

We conducted a targeted scoping review of 13 CE-certified AI systems for autonomous or semi-autonomous DR detection available in the European Union as of October 23, 2025 (IDx-DR, EyeArt, RetCAD, Mona DR, Retmarker DR, SELENA+, Remidio Medios AI, RetinoScan, Aireen DR, OphthAI, LuxIA, Airdoc-Eye DR, and Vistel). Data were charted across predefined domains, including device designation, regulatory classification, evidence sources, validation study design, reported diagnostic performance metrics, and implementation-related considerations. The review aimed to map the extent and nature of available evidence without conducting quantitative synthesis or comparative ranking.

Results

Most systems employed deep-learning-based fundus image analysis, often incorporating automated image-quality assessment. Reported sensitivities and specificities for referable DR (RDR) varied across systems, generally falling within ranges consistent with regulatory expectations; however, reporting standards and study designs were heterogeneous, limiting direct comparison. Several systems were supported by multicenter or prospective evaluations, while others relied primarily on retrospective datasets. A subset of platforms reported multi-disease detection capabilities. Evidence specific to sight-threatening DR (STDR) was less frequently described and demonstrated wider variability. Non-EU regulatory pathways were mentioned in some reports, but were outside the primary scope of this review. Other systems demonstrate high diagnostic accuracy in controlled evaluations, though performance for STDR remains limited (mean ≈ 80%), largely due to reliance on single-modality 2D fundus imaging without optical coherence tomography (OCT) integration. Implementation-related evidence, including workflow integration and monitoring requirements under the EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR), was limited across systems.

Conclusions

CE-certified AI systems for DR detection represent a diverse and rapidly evolving landscape. While substantial progress has been made in regulatory classification and validation efforts, evidence remains heterogeneous, particularly for STDR detection and real-world implementation. Future research should prioritize consistent reporting standards, evaluation of multimodal approaches, and studies addressing real-world effectiveness to support safe and equitable deployment under the evolving EU regulatory framework.

records.title: Sensor-Based Technologies for the Detection of Unwanted Loneliness in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.

content.title: Sensor-Based Technologies for the Detection of Unwanted Loneliness in Older Adults: A Systematic Review.
content.abstract: Background: Unwanted loneliness and social isolation in older adults are public health problems with negative effects on physical and mental health. The usual assessment tools, based on self-report questionnaires, have limitations in capturing these phenomena continuously and objectively. Objective: We aimed to critically analyze recent scientific evidence on the use of passive sensor technologies combined with artificial intelligence for the detection of unwanted loneliness and social isolation in older adults. Methods: Studies were reviewed in databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore) that used wearable devices, environmental sensors in the home, smartphones, and multimodal fusion approaches. This systematic review was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Results: Behavioral variables derived from passive monitoring, such as mobility, time away from home, sleep patterns, and digital interactions, are consistently associated with measures of loneliness and social isolation. Likewise, artificial intelligence models based on the combination of multiple data sources show better predictive performance than unimodal approaches. Conclusions: Sensor-based technologies can complement traditional assessment methods, although their practical application requires overcoming challenges related to methodological validation, user acceptance, and ethical considerations.

records.title: Pericoronary adipose tissue imaging: quantitative assessment, artificial intelligence integration, and therapeutic modulation.

content.title: Pericoronary adipose tissue imaging: quantitative assessment, artificial intelligence integration, and therapeutic modulation.
content.abstract: Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) is increasingly recognised as a biosensor of vascular inflammation. The guideline-driven widespread adoption of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) as the first-line investigation for coronary artery disease (CAD) has created opportunities for evaluating the inflammatory burden through quantitative assessment of PCAT. Standardising raw PCAT imaging data for technical, anatomical, and biological variability provides the Fat-Attenuation Index (FAI) Score, which shows promise as a metric of coronary inflammation. Quantification of coronary inflammation has implications for the diagnosis, risk stratification, and monitoring of treatment in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This review examines the anatomical and physiological basis of PCAT, highlighting the importance of standardising PCAT imaging for the implementation as a clinical biomarker, and reviews the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing precision and scalability. Emerging evidence on the modulation of FAI Score by therapeutic agents, including statins, biologics, and cardiometabolic drugs, and the potential utility of serial imaging in guiding clinical care is also discussed. With ongoing large-scale validation and emerging AI -based approaches, PCAT imaging is poised to complement traditional risk factors and plaque metrics; however, current evidence remains evolving, and the integration of inflammatory risk assessment could be useful to guide emerging anti-inflammatory treatments in personalised cardiovascular medicine.

records.title: Effect of menstrual cups on vaginal health, reproductive tract and urogenital infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
